title: China's urban population reached 67 percent in 2024
content: China's National Bureau of Statistics reported 943.50 million urban permanent residents at the end of 2024, representing 67.0 percent of the population. Urban living contexts therefore require explicit coverage in product forecasting.
source_name: National Bureau of Statistics of China

title: China has a large and growing older population segment
content: The 2024 national statistical communiqué reported that people aged 60 and above represented 22.0 percent of the population and people aged 65 and above represented 15.6 percent.
source_name: National Bureau of Statistics of China

title: Old urban residential community renovation affects millions of households
content: China's 2024 statistical communiqué reported that renovation began in 58,000 old urban residential communities, benefiting 9.66 million households. Retrofit-friendly installation is therefore a relevant design constraint.
source_name: National Bureau of Statistics of China

title: PIPL requires lawful and necessary personal-information processing
content: China's Personal Information Protection Law protects personal-information rights and regulates collection, storage, use, transmission, disclosure and deletion. Processing must be lawful, necessary and for a justified purpose.

title: Network data rules add personal-information obligations
content: China's Regulations on Network Data Security Management include a dedicated chapter on personal-information protection, making data governance a product architecture issue rather than only a policy document.

title: Urban household income provides a price-context anchor
content: The National Bureau of Statistics reported per-capita disposable income of urban households at 54,188 yuan in 2024. This is a macro context signal, not direct evidence of willingness to pay for home security.
source_name: National Bureau of Statistics of China

title: Apartment entry and shared corridors create boundary ambiguity
content: In dense residential buildings, the private front door meets a shared corridor managed alongside neighbors and property services. Sensing scope, bystander privacy and installation permission require local validation.

title: Compact non-destructive retrofit may lower adoption friction
content: For rented or renovated urban apartments, small devices using adhesive or existing fixtures may be easier to adopt than new wiring. This product assumption requires installation testing with residents and property managers.

title: Property-management integration creates both leverage and dependency
content: A building-level security concept may gain distribution or response value through property management, while creating procurement, interoperability and responsibility dependencies. Both direct-to-consumer and property-assisted paths need validation.
